html:
SMTO-EXE-0191 — The PDF tools on this Gateway need repair

GUID: 5bbfc24a-9fd0-50f2-be11-275a2720cb20
Slug: pdf-backend-unavailable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: pdf

What happened

  • The computer running the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to work with files there) is missing the PDF software SMTO needs, or has the wrong version of it. No PDF was opened or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Note which Gateway this task uses (the computer chosen for the task in the message box), and tell the person who manages that computer that its PDF tools need repair. The missing PDF software is on that specific computer, so the repair must happen there.
  2. On that computer, once running tasks have finished, run the SMTO installer again as the same user account that runs the Gateway. The installer puts back the correct PDF software and checks that it works.
  3. After the installer finishes without errors, restart the Gateway or that computer and check it shows Connected in Settings › Setup › Gateways. The Gateway only picks up repaired software after it starts again.
  4. Start a new task and ask for the PDF step again. Older tasks remember what the Gateway could do when they started and won't see the repair.

What success looks like

  • In a new task, SMTO opens the PDF and finishes the step.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, along with any errors the installer showed. Don't remove or re-pair the Gateway or delete its settings; repairing the installation in place is enough. Giving a Skill permission does not install the software it needs.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected Gateway is missing a compatible PDF backend (pypdf 6.19–<7 or pypdfium2 5.x), or the installer's import or functional check for it failed; the installation needs repair.

What this means

  • PDF backend readiness found a failed backend verification or an installed parser/renderer dependency outside its supported compatibility range. PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.

Why this can happen

  • PDF backend readiness found a failed backend verification or an installed parser/renderer dependency outside its supported compatibility range.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the named parser/renderer readiness under the selected Gateway account, not the controller's installation.

How to fix it

  • Reinstall or repair the affected Gateway by rerunning its supported installer on that Gateway host, as the account used by the Gateway: ./install.sh (server plus local Gateway), ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh (Linux), ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh (macOS) or .\src\gateway_windows\install.ps1 (Windows); require its dependency audit and functional checks to pass (pypdf 6.19 to below 7, pypdfium2 5.x). After active work settles, restart the Gateway (and the server if the shared installer updated it), refresh Gateway metadata, confirm it advertises pdf_structure and pdf_render, and start a new task, because existing tasks keep their captured capability snapshot. Do not delete Gateway pairing, credentials, settings, browser profiles or task artifacts.
  • Reinstall or repair the affected Gateway by rerunning its supported installer on that Gateway host. After installation succeeds and active work is settled, restart the Gateway and refresh its metadata.
  • From the matching repository checkout, run ./install.sh for the server and local Gateway, or use the Gateway-only installer: ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh on Linux, ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh on macOS, or .\src\gateway_windows\install.ps1 on Windows. Run it as the account used by the Gateway so its environment and browser caches are repaired.
  • After active jobs and uncertain operations are reconciled, restart the affected Gateway. Restart the server too if the shared installer updated it. Refresh Gateway metadata before starting a new task.
  • Require the installer dependency audit and local functional checks to pass, then verify the selected Gateway advertises the required capability. Start a new task after refreshing metadata; existing tasks retain their captured capability snapshot.

Retry and execution caution

  • Require the installer dependency audit and local functional checks to pass, then verify the selected Gateway advertises the required capability. Start a new task after refreshing metadata; existing tasks retain their captured capability snapshot. Inspect prior execution receipts before repeating work.

How to verify the fix

  • The affected PDF backend passes supported installation verification and advertises readiness.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.
  • Repair the installation in place; do not delete Gateway pairing, credentials, settings, browser profiles or task artifacts.
  • Granting a Skill permission does not install its dependencies.

Technical notes

  • PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
